thought.text: The pkill pattern matched my own shell. Let me check what state the processes are in now:

reasoning_content: Exit code 143 (SIGTERM) suggests that pkill -f matched its own shell command line (which contains "webpack" in the grep pattern text), causing the shell to terminate. Let's check the current state: is the webpack dev server still running? Did the Python server terminate? Let's check the ports and processes again.

action.command: ps aux | grep -vE 'grep|ps aux' | grep -E 'webpack|http.server|node' ; echo "---"; for f in /proc/net/tcp /proc/net/tcp6; do [ -f "$f" ] && awk 'NR>1 && $4=="0A" {split($2,a,":"); printf "%d\n", ("0x" a[2])+0}' "$f"; done | sort -un

tool_call.name: terminal
tool_call.arguments: {"command": "ps aux | grep -vE 'grep|ps aux' | grep -E 'webpack|http.server|node' ; echo \"---\"; for f in /proc/net/tcp /proc/net/tcp6; do [ -f \"$f\" ] && awk 'NR>1 && $4==\"0A\" {split($2,a,\":\"); printf \"%d\\n\", (\"0x\" a[2])+0}' \"$f\"; done | sort -un", "security_risk": "LOW", "summary": "Check remaining node/webpack processes and ports"}
